output.summary: An herbaceous perennial native to China, Japan, Korea and Sakhalin, it bears male and female flowers on separate plants, although sterile flowers with both forms occasionally occur. Its shoots are traditionally treated to reduce harshness before being fried, steamed or boiled.
output.edibilityNote: Shoots are eaten after treatments such as soaking, boiling or frying; the plant contains liver-toxic and carcinogenic pyrrolizidine alkaloids.
